title: How sharp is the bend?
hook: Same 2 m cord, coiled in loops twice as wide.

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that a tighter coil bends the cord more sharply, and doubling the loop radius halves how sharply it bends

misconception: However you coil a cord, the bend is the same because it is the same cord.
objective: A circle’s curvature is the reciprocal of its radius. A larger-radius loop uses more length per turn and bends less sharply; neither the cord material nor total length changes.

recall.question: You coil a cord in loops of 15 cm radius instead of 30 cm. What happens to its curvature?
options: It stays the same: same cord
recall.why: Curvature = 1 ÷ radius. Half the radius gives twice the curvature, a sharper bend, and each turn uses less cord. The card gives no product-specific bend limit.
